alerts.title: Carbamazepine reduces DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir (DTG) levels by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid as an alternative anti-epileptic. The patient is on DTG-based ART (TLD) and started carbamazepine two weeks ago. The current viral load is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This timing suggests a drug-drug interaction may be causing virologic failure. The clinician's plan does not address this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Address the drug interaction per guidelines. Consider switching from carbamazepine to valproic acid or adjusting the DTG dosing.

alerts.title: Viral load >50 requires action
alerts.message: Guidelines for patients on DTG-based ART state that a viral load (VL) >50 copies/mL requires enhanced adherence support, addressing side-effects affecting adherence, and a repeat VL in 2-3 months. The patient's VL is 1,240 copies/mL. The clinician's plan only notes the detectable VL and is unsure of the cause, but does not outline the guideline-mandated steps for management.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address potential side-effects, and schedule a repeat viral load test in 2-3 months as per the algorithm.

alerts.title: Hyponatremia with carbamazepine
alerts.message: The patient has symptomatic carbamazepine toxicity (level 14 mcg/mL) with neurological signs and a low sodium of 128 mmol/L. Hyponatremia is a known adverse effect of carbamazepine. The clinician's plan to reduce the dose and repeat the level is appropriate but does not mention managing the electrolyte imbalance.

evidence.recommended_action: Manage carbamazepine toxicity per standard care: dose reduction, monitor sodium, and assess for need to correct hyponatremia.
